about: The dismissal after the last prayer following Communion. The priest greets the faithful and says “Ite, missa est”, answered by “Deo grátias”. When a procession follows the Mass he says “Benedicámus Dómino” instead, and in Masses for the Dead “Requiéscant in pace”, answered by “Amen”.

s01.narrative: After the last prayer following Communion the priest says:

s04.narrative: Turned toward the people, the priest says “Ite, missa est”, and the server answers “Deo grátias”. When a liturgical procession follows the Mass, he says “Benedicámus Dómino” instead, at the middle of the altar, facing it.

s05.translation: Go forth, the Mass is ended.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s07.narrative: In Masses for the Dead the priest says instead, facing the altar: Requiéscant in pace — and the answer is Amen.

w008.note: As a noun, “missa” means dismissal. The same form can be a participle of “mitto,” meaning “sent.” A participial reading would require an understood subject that the formula does not name.

w011.explanation: The response leaves the verb unspoken. Its full sense is “we give thanks to God”.
